annotation.title_clean: Increasing Access to Data Across the Economy
annotation.title_en: Increasing Access to Data Across the Economy
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Frontier Economics Ltd (for Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport)
annotation.venue: GOV.UK (published with National AI Strategy HTML version page)
annotation.summary_en: Frontier Economics report for DCMS (March 2021) proposing a five-step framework to prioritise government interventions that increase data access and sharing across the UK economy. It identifies six data-sharing issues and six policy levers, with an initial market sizing and case studies. Not about AI or robotics directly.
key_provisions_or_claims: Five-step framework: rationales, data-sharing issues, levers, economic activity sizing, effectiveness assessment.
Six data-sharing issues: incentives, knowledge, regulatory/legal risk, costs, commercial/ethical risk, missed public-interest uses.
Six levers: knowledge, data foundations, risk-addressing solutions, incentives, reduced regulatory burden, mandated sharing.
Addressing risk and reducing costs likely affect the most economic activity directly.
Evidence base is sparse; conclusions are preliminary.
